# Evidence
- Problem class: go-config-boot-refusal-borrowed-registry
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-10-16T13:48:25.386Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description: bunkerd scratch daemon with a private --config set its own agent.base_data_dir but left agent.registry.path unset, so the compiled default /var/lib/bunkerd/agents.jsonl applied: the daemon replayed the PRODUCTION registry (11497 events, 5 live agents) and began DESTROYING live agent 4355af2b within 60s of boot. Approach that worked: do NOT touch reconcile/destroy and do NOT build the gate on the registry flock (lockCrossProcess is held only for a write, so it proves nothing about a live owner). Mirror the existing DF-BUNKER-95 gate instead: a pure read-only config predicate that refuses boot when (1) agent.base_data_dir is set and != the default dir, (2) the resolved registry path (empty falls back to DefaultRegistryPath) is INSIDE the default dir via pathWithinDir, and (3) the default tree already holds the owning daemon's registry file AND its instance identity file; fail OPEN on missing/unreadable evidence (os.Stat error means not proven). Wire it at BOTH boot call sites next to the existing gate with the same fmt.Errorf wrapping prefix and keep the error text free of that prefix so the wrap adds it exactly once. Hermetic tests take the default dir as a parameter and pass a scratch temp dir; the incident shape (unset registry path) can only be proven structurally - pin DefaultRegistryPath == DefaultAgentBaseDataDir + /agents.jsonl and add the equivalent explicit-path refusal case - because a temp-dir test cannot seed the real /var/lib/bunkerd.
